units.text: INT. PYGMALION - CONTINUOUS
You said it was.
units.name: MRS. HIGGINS

units.text: Not your part of it. I’ve picked up a girl.
units.name: HIGGINS

units.text: Does that mean that some girl has picked you up?
units.name: MRS. HIGGINS

units.text: Not at all. I don’t mean a love affair.
units.name: HIGGINS

units.text: What a pity!
units.name: MRS. HIGGINS

units.text: Why?
units.name: HIGGINS

units.text: Well, you never fall in love with anyone under forty-five. When will you discover that there are some rather nice-looking young women about?
units.name: MRS. HIGGINS

units.text: Oh, I can’t be bothered with young women. My idea of a loveable woman is something as like you as possible. I shall never get into the way of seriously liking young women: some habits lie too deep to be changed.
units.name: HIGGINS

units.text: Rising abruptly and walking about, jingling his money and his keys in his trouser pockets.
Besides, they’re all idiots.
units.name: HIGGINS

units.text: Do you know what you would do if you really loved me, Henry?
units.name: MRS. HIGGINS

units.text: Oh bother! What? Marry, I suppose?
units.name: HIGGINS

units.text: No. Stop fidgeting and take your hands out of your pockets.
units.name: MRS. HIGGINS

units.text: With a gesture of despair, he obeys and sits down again.
That’s a good boy. Now tell me about the girl.
units.name: MRS. HIGGINS

units.text: She’s coming to see you.
units.name: HIGGINS

units.text: I don’t remember asking her.
units.name: MRS. HIGGINS

units.text: You didn’t. I asked her. If you’d known her you wouldn’t have asked her.
units.name: HIGGINS

units.text: Indeed! Why?
units.name: MRS. HIGGINS

units.text: Well, it’s like this. She’s a common flower girl. I picked her off the kerbstone.
units.name: HIGGINS

units.text: And invited her to my at-home!
units.name: MRS. HIGGINS

units.text: HIGGINS [rising and coming to her to coax her] Oh, that’ll be all right.
I’ve taught her to speak properly; and she has strict orders as to her behavior.
She’s to keep to two subjects: the weather and everybody’s health—Fine day and How do you do, you know—and not to let herself go on things in general.
That will be safe.
Safe! To talk about our health! about our insides! perhaps about our outsides! How could you be so silly, Henry?
units.name: MRS. HIGGINS

units.text: HIGGINS [impatiently] Well, she must talk about something. [He controls himself and sits down again].
Oh, she’ll be all right: don’t you fuss.
Pickering is in it with me.
I’ve a sort of bet on that I’ll pass her off as a duchess in six months.
I started on her some months ago; and she’s getting on like a house on fire.
I shall win my bet.
She has a quick ear; and she’s been easier to teach than my middle-class pupils because she’s had to learn a complete new language.
She talks English almost as you talk French.
That’s satisfactory, at all events.
units.name: MRS. HIGGINS

units.text: Well, it is and it isn’t.
units.name: HIGGINS

units.text: What does that mean?
units.name: MRS. HIGGINS

units.text: You see, I’ve got her pronunciation all right; but you have to consider not only how a girl pronounces, but what she pronounces; and that’s where—
units.name: HIGGINS

units.text: They are interrupted by the parlor-maid, announcing guests.
Mrs. and Miss Eynsford Hill.
units.name: THE PARLOR-MAID

units.text: She withdraws.
Oh Lord!
units.name: HIGGINS

units.text: He rises; snatches his hat from the table; and makes for the door; but before he reaches it his mother introduces him.
Mrs. and Miss Eynsford Hill are the mother and daughter who sheltered from the rain in Covent Garden.
The mother is well bred, quiet, and has the habitual anxiety of straitened means.
The daughter has acquired a gay air of being very much at home in society: the bravado of genteel poverty.
EYNSFORD HILL
units.name: MRS

units.text: to Mrs. Higgins.
How do you do?
units.name: MRS

units.text: They shake hands.
How d’you do?
units.name: MISS EYNSFORD HILL

units.text: She shakes.
HIGGINS
units.name: MRS

units.text: introducing.
My son Henry.
units.name: MRS

units.text: Your celebrated son! I have so longed to meet you, Professor Higgins.
units.name: MRS. EYNSFORD HILL

units.text: HIGGINS [glumly, making no movement in her direction] Delighted. [He backs against the piano and bows brusquely].
